objectives: Decode familiar CVC words containing the newly taught /p/ grapheme.
Blend /p/ with known m, s, t and short-a sounds.
Notice whether /p/ occurs at the beginning or end of a word.
concepts: New graphemes become useful when integrated with secure previous correspondences.
Position changes the phoneme sequence even when the same grapheme is used.
Accurate decoding requires checking every grapheme.

definitions.definition: Combining individual phonemes smoothly to pronounce a whole word.

workedExamples: pat vs sat → initial phoneme changes
map vs mat → final phoneme changes
commonMistakes: Guessing a familiar word instead of reading all graphemes.

conceptual: Compare words with /p/ in different positions.
application: Decode new combinations using taught graphemes.
higherOrderThinking: Diagnose whether an error came from the first or final phoneme.
mixedReview: Sound, blend, compare and reread CVC words with p.

formulaOrFactBank: CVC decoding = grapheme → phoneme → blend → word
mistakeBasedRevision: If pat is read as sat, check the initial sound; if map is read as mat, check the final sound.
weakTopicRevision: Practise mixed initial/final /p/ CVC words with immediate rereading after errors.

activities.name: Position sort
steps: Identify whether /p/ is first or final.

outcomes: Learner decodes at least 8 of 10 familiar CVC words containing p.
Learner accurately identifies /p/ in initial and final positions.
Learner blends three-phoneme sequences without omitting the middle vowel.

Which word can be blended from /m/ /a/ /p/?
Which word can be blended from /t/ /a/ /p/?
What should you do first when decoding a new CVC word?
options: Look at each grapheme and say its sound

questions.question: Which word has /p/ as its first sound?
Which word has /p/ as its final sound?
Which word is different from the others because /p/ is not present?
A learner reads 'pat' as 'sat'. Which sound should they check?
A learner reads 'map' as 'mat'. Which sound should they check?
Which sequence is correct for decoding 'tap'?
Why is blending useful after saying the separate sounds?
options: It combines the sounds into the spoken word

questions.question: Which activity gives useful /p/ decoding practice?
options: Read pat, map and tap by sounding and blending

questions.question: What shows secure /p/ decoding?
options: The learner accurately decodes familiar CVC words with p in different positions
The learner guesses p-words from pictures
The learner names p without reading words
